data.title: When we get Komooted
data.author: atakan_gurkan
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要介绍了 bikepacking 网站提供的各类资源和服务，包括探索路线、灵感故事、旅行计划、装备推荐等。网站拥有超过300条全球各地的bikepacking路线，并提供详细的GPS地图和摄影作品。用户可以按地点、路线类型和时长筛选路线，还可以加入Bikepacking Collective以获取更多内容和《Bikepacking Journal》杂志。

文章还讨论了Komoot平台被出售给私人股权公司后对社区的影响，揭露了此次出售对员工和用户的负面影响，强调了企业资本与社区之间的矛盾。

总结来说，文章提供了丰富的bikepacking信息和资源，同时警示了社区平台商业化可能带来的问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Komoot公司出售及其对员工和用户的影响

不同观点：
• **员工被剥削和公司背叛感**：[dakiol]认为员工为了Komoot的使命接受了低薪和生活变动，但最终被解雇，而高层却获得了巨额收益。这种经历让[dakiol]决定在工作中不再付出额外努力，并每隔2-3年更换工作以最大化收入。[BozeWolf]也表达了对被解雇员工的同情，并提到自己对Komoot应用的信任度下降，担心服务质量会下降。

• **寻找替代应用**：[BozeWolf]表示尽管对Komoot不满，但目前仍依赖该应用，并希望被解雇的员工能开发出替代应用。如果有人知道其他替代品，希望能推荐。[farfromrefuge]回应称自己已经开发了一个开源的替代应用AlpiMaps，并提供了相关链接和使用说明。

• **公司出售对用户和员工的影响**：[StrLght]对员工的遭遇表示同情，但认为用户可以找到替代应用。[pentamassiv]则对公司声称“永不销售”表示怀疑，并建议用户不要相信公司所谓的社区归属感。[thomasahle]则探讨了是否有公司形式可以防止此类出售行为，比如非营利组织或公共利益公司。

• **情感投入与法律问题**：[padjo]认为员工不应将个人使命与公司绑定，尤其是在没有股权的情况下。[demosito666]质疑员工为何对一个以盈利为目的的公司产生情感投入，除非该公司对“更大利益”有贡献。[johnecheck]则从法律角度提出，员工可能有违约索赔的权利，尤其是在公司出售与其承诺不符的情况下。

• **面试经历与公司文化**：[baxuz]分享了多年前面试Komoot的不愉快经历，并对公司文化提出批评。[ramon156]表示庆幸自己当年被Komoot拒绝，认为这样避免了进入一个糟糕的工作环境。

• **对文章论点的批评**：[Fade_Dance]认为文章中对生成式AI和资本的批评存在矛盾，并指出文章的论点需要更多推敲。[avhception]则对Komoot的遭遇表示冷漠，认为自己坚持使用OpenStreetMap是正确的选择。[xandrius]建议用户在看到喜爱的应用被Bending Spoons收购时应立即离开。

补充讨论：
• **公司诚信与法律保护**：[ndkap]质疑是否有法律手段确保公司遵守“永不销售”的承诺，并认为仅凭公司口头承诺是不明智的。

• **开源与社区驱动项目的优势**：[farfromrefuge]提供的AlpiMaps是一个开源项目，强调了其离线功能和自定义地图生成的能力，但同时也提到目前用户群小，可能存在较多bug。

争议焦点：
• 公司是否有责任遵守“永不销售”的承诺，以及如何在法律上保障员工和用户的权益。
• 员工是否应将个人使命与公司绑定，尤其是在没有股权的情况下。
• 对生成式AI和资本的双重标准批评是否合理。

Imagine going for a ride on your favorite loop through your local woods and stumbling upon a notice of an impending clear-cut. That’s the shock many of us in the European cycling community felt when the news broke that our trusted route platform, Komoot, was sold to the notorious private equity group Bending Spoons on March 20th of this year. Breaking their promise of long-term commitment to the company, Komoot’s six founders sold out the around 150 employees, millions of active users, and the beloved service, making off with the lion’s share of the 300-million-euro deal.
1
The employees were the first to get the axe. They signed in one morning to learn that the company many had dedicated up to 15 years of their life to was no more. Eighty percent were fired immediately. I spoke with a few longtime employees in the aftermath, who described it as a rough and cruel betrayal.

44699421.article_summary:
这篇文章主要介绍了 bikepacking 网站提供的各类资源和服务，包括探索路线、灵感故事、旅行计划、装备推荐等。网站拥有超过300条全球各地的bikepacking路线，并提供详细的GPS地图和摄影作品。用户可以按地点、路线类型和时长筛选路线，还可以加入Bikepacking Collective以获取更多内容和《Bikepacking Journal》杂志。

文章还讨论了Komoot平台被出售给私人股权公司后对社区的影响，揭露了此次出售对员工和用户的负面影响，强调了企业资本与社区之间的矛盾。

总结来说，文章提供了丰富的bikepacking信息和资源，同时警示了社区平台商业化可能带来的问题。

不同观点：
• **员工被剥削和公司背叛感**：[dakiol]认为员工为了Komoot的使命接受了低薪和生活变动，但最终被解雇，而高层却获得了巨额收益。这种经历让[dakiol]决定在工作中不再付出额外努力，并每隔2-3年更换工作以最大化收入。[BozeWolf]也表达了对被解雇员工的同情，并提到自己对Komoot应用的信任度下降，担心服务质量会下降。

• **寻找替代应用**：[BozeWolf]表示尽管对Komoot不满，但目前仍依赖该应用，并希望被解雇的员工能开发出替代应用。如果有人知道其他替代品，希望能推荐。[farfromrefuge]回应称自己已经开发了一个开源的替代应用AlpiMaps，并提供了相关链接和使用说明。

• **公司出售对用户和员工的影响**：[StrLght]对员工的遭遇表示同情，但认为用户可以找到替代应用。[pentamassiv]则对公司声称“永不销售”表示怀疑，并建议用户不要相信公司所谓的社区归属感。[thomasahle]则探讨了是否有公司形式可以防止此类出售行为，比如非营利组织或公共利益公司。

• **情感投入与法律问题**：[padjo]认为员工不应将个人使命与公司绑定，尤其是在没有股权的情况下。[demosito666]质疑员工为何对一个以盈利为目的的公司产生情感投入，除非该公司对“更大利益”有贡献。[johnecheck]则从法律角度提出，员工可能有违约索赔的权利，尤其是在公司出售与其承诺不符的情况下。

• **面试经历与公司文化**：[baxuz]分享了多年前面试Komoot的不愉快经历，并对公司文化提出批评。[ramon156]表示庆幸自己当年被Komoot拒绝，认为这样避免了进入一个糟糕的工作环境。

• **对文章论点的批评**：[Fade_Dance]认为文章中对生成式AI和资本的批评存在矛盾，并指出文章的论点需要更多推敲。[avhception]则对Komoot的遭遇表示冷漠，认为自己坚持使用OpenStreetMap是正确的选择。[xandrius]建议用户在看到喜爱的应用被Bending Spoons收购时应立即离开。

补充讨论：
• **公司诚信与法律保护**：[ndkap]质疑是否有法律手段确保公司遵守“永不销售”的承诺，并认为仅凭公司口头承诺是不明智的。

• **开源与社区驱动项目的优势**：[farfromrefuge]提供的AlpiMaps是一个开源项目，强调了其离线功能和自定义地图生成的能力，但同时也提到目前用户群小，可能存在较多bug。

争议焦点：
• 公司是否有责任遵守“永不销售”的承诺，以及如何在法律上保障员工和用户的权益。
• 员工是否应将个人使命与公司绑定，尤其是在没有股权的情况下。
• 对生成式AI和资本的双重标准批评是否合理。

data.title: Show HN: Open-source physical rack-mounted GUI for home lab
data.author: mmajzoobi
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一个专为自托管服务和家庭实验室设计的Raspberry Pi控制界面模块。该模块可以安装在迷你或全尺寸机架上，支持无头（headless）控制和系统资源、应用程序状态的监控。作者之前在一个开源项目Ubo pod中设计了此GUI，并决定将其独立出来作为一个单独模块使用。新的设计包括一个PCB和外壳，以适应机架安装，并且正在尝试增加倾斜显示设计。软件部分已相对成熟，可以在网页浏览器中试用。作者欢迎用户提供反馈以改进设计。所有设计文件和代码均在GitHub上开源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub项目"geerlingguy/mini-rack"中关于硬件兼容性和项目维护的问题。

不同观点：
• **mmajzoobi的观点**：提供了一些额外的背景信息，试图帮助理解问题的上下文。他提到了一个具体的GitHub issue链接（#229），可能对解决问题有帮助。他认为通过查看该issue可以更好地理解当前遇到的硬件兼容性问题。

• **geerlingguy的观点**：项目维护者提到，当前项目是基于特定硬件环境开发的，可能不支持所有硬件配置。他指出，某些硬件组件（如特定的Raspberry Pi型号）并不在项目的支持范围内，因此可能无法正常工作。他强调项目文档中已明确列出支持的硬件，并建议用户参考这些信息。

• **其他用户（多个评论者）的观点**：一些用户报告了类似的硬件兼容性问题，特别是在使用Raspberry Pi 4时。他们指出，即使按照文档操作，仍然遇到无法识别或错误配置的问题。这些用户希望项目能够扩展支持更多的硬件型号，或者提供更详细的故障排查指南。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：项目是否应扩展其硬件支持范围，或者是否应在现有范围内严格限制支持的硬件。一些用户认为项目应更具包容性，以适应更广泛的硬件环境，而项目维护者则强调资源有限，只能保证支持文档中列出的硬件。

• **技术细节**：讨论中涉及具体的技术细节，如设备的电源要求、USB接口兼容性等。部分用户提供了自己尝试过的解决方案和变通方法，但这些方法并未被所有用户验证成功。

• **维护者建议**：geerlingguy建议用户在遇到问题时提交详细的bug报告，并提供相关日志，以便更好地排查问题。他还提到，社区贡献是项目改进的重要途径，欢迎有能力的用户提交兼容性补丁。

44704742.article_content:
The enclosure mounts as a 2U unit. 1U form factor was a bit challenging to pull off but I can try again.
I have realized that a lot of people nowadays self-host services and set up home labs with mini racks.
Image from
https://mini-rack.jeffgeerling.com/
A significant challenge I've personally encountered is quickly obtaining health status from self-hosted services and machines, along with having the capability to control my Raspberry Pi headlessly within a mini rack.
So, it got me thinking about creating a built-in GUI that users can easily add to their Raspberry Pi nodes. This would be suitable for mini or full racks, or even other locations.
I have previously designed this GUI for an open source project I have been working on (called Ubo pod:
github.com/ubopod/
) and decided to detach/decouple the GUI into its own standalone module for this use case.
So this is roughly how it is going to look like:
3D view of the rack mount GUI
The GUI enables headless control of your Raspberry Pi, along with monitoring of system resources and application status. The image below summarizes its capabilities.
Summary of what you can do with the GUI
I am designing a new PCB and enclosure as part of this re-design to allow for a new form factor that mounts on server racks (mini or full rack).
standalone GUI module
This modularization and decoupling can also enable me to quickly iterate on other design concepts for future designs of Ubo pod and its accessories.
For example, I am playing around with a design that tilts the display/GUI for a better viewing angle.
Ubo Pod concept design with tilted display
I am recording my journey of re-designing this and I would love to get early feedback from users to better understand what they may need or require from such a solution, specially on the hardware side. You can watch the first part of the video here:
Design process of GUI module (Part 1)
The software behind the GUI is quite mature (
github.com/ubopod/ubo_app
) and you can actually try it right now without the hardware inside the web browser as shown in the video.
This video walks you through the steps needs to run the GUI on a bare Raspberry Pi:
Running Ubo App and GUI on bare Raspberry Pi with no additional hardware requires.
All PCB designs are available here:
github.com/ubopod/ubo-pcb
If you have any suggestions or feedback on the design, please comment below and let me know.

data.title: Shallow water is dangerous too
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者一家在度假时，他四岁的女儿在浅水喷泉中险些溺水的事件。尽管喷泉水深较浅，仅到孩子肘部，且有成人看护，但孩子仍因穿着蓬松的裙子或缺乏水中平衡能力而无法站立，导致头部浸入水中。幸亏作者的姨妈及时发现并呼救，作者迅速救起孩子，孩子最终平安无事。作者反思了自己的疏忽，认识到浅水并不等同于无风险，特别是对小孩而言，意外和慌乱可能导致危险。他感到庆幸的同时也自责，提醒家长们对任何水体都应保持警惕。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：儿童与水相关的安全问题，特别是如何防止溺水以及游泳教育的重要性。

不同观点：
• qchris认为，汽车、狗和水是儿童日常生活中三大可能造成严重伤害的因素，尤其水危险难以预见。他强调严格的规则和早期游泳课程的重要性。
• ncruces指出，在葡萄牙，游泳教育在小学中被强调以减少溺水事故，并提到该国在减少溺水方面的进步。
• grujicd分享了个人经历，警示即使在看似安全的条件下（如使用游泳圈），儿童仍可能面临溺水风险。
• susiecambria讲述了自己在水中遇险的经历，并强调了对水保持高度警惕的重要性，尤其是在监督儿童时。
• burnt-resistor建议对所有低于1米的静水设置围栏，并提到低水头坝和洪水区域的危险性。
• RyanOD提醒家长，儿童落水时可能毫无声响，家长需时刻保持警惕。
• chrismatheson重申了小水体（如积水）的潜在危险，并基于自身潜水经验强调对水的敬畏。
• chmod775认为，儿童在学会走路的同时就能学会不惊慌并保持头部在水面以上，3-5岁时可以学会独立游泳，这为父母提供了安心。
• jcalx引用了相关公共安全警告，指出溺水通常是悄无声息的事件，而非人们想象中的大喊大叫和挥手。
• ghaff提到某些大学要求通过游泳测试才能毕业，虽然对于幼儿不适用，但认为游泳技能很重要。
• praptak强调即使小水体（如拖地桶）也可能导致致命事故。
• plasma_beam作为泳池拥有者和家长，认为不应让幼儿在没有监督的情况下接近任何水体，无论水深多少。
• eviks质疑是否可以通过教授游泳来避免这些危险。
• littlestymaar通过实例指出，即使是极浅的水体（23厘米）也可能导致儿童溺亡。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否通过早期游泳教育和严格的监督可以有效防止儿童溺水事故的发生。
• 个人经历被广泛引用以强调水危险的无处不在以及不同情况下溺水的可能性。
• 对水体（包括浅水和静水）设置物理屏障（如围栏）的建议也被讨论，以作为防止儿童接近水体的实际措施。
• 对水危险的无形性和突发性是讨论中反复出现的主题，许多评论者强调了持续监督和早期安全教育的重要性。

Shallow Water is Dangerous Too
July 19th, 2025
kids
Content warning: risk to children
Julia and I
know
drowning is the
biggest
risk to US kids 1-4
, and we try to take this seriously.
But yesterday our 4yo came very close to drowning in a
fountain. (She's fine now.)
This week we were on vacation with my extended family: nine kids,
eight parents, and ten grandparents/uncles/aunts.  For the last few
years we've been in a series of rental houses, and this time on
arrival we found a fountain in the backyard:
I immediately checked the depth with a stick and found that it would
be just below the elbows on our 4yo.  I think it was likely 24" deep;
any deeper and PA
would
require a fence
.  I talked with Julia and other parents, and
reasoned that since it was within standing depth it was safe.
We discussed boundaries with the kids (no going through the gate or
out the driveway, stay within the fence, stay out of the pond) and
then let them play on their own.  They were in and out of the house
all week and, while with this many people around they were rarely
alone, we also weren't ensuring they were accompanied.
Yesterday evening my aunt noticed our 4yo was walking on the fountain
rim, and called me over to say this looked dangerous.  Checking, I
initially didn't see her at all.  Then, in an image burned into my
mind, I saw the top of her head moving in the water.  I sprinted over,
jumped in, and despite the shallow depth immediately fell full in:
very slippery on the bottom.  Still, I got her out quickly, and to my
relief she was breathing, normal-colored, and immediately started
crying.
With the timing of my aunt's warning and how long it took me to get
there, I think she was likely in for about fifteen seconds.  It seems
she held her breath and didn't take in any water.
After she recovered she told me she was trying to push her legs down
and stand up, but they wouldn't go down.  I don't know if the problem
was that she was wearing a very poofy dress (pictured below), or
that she doesn't have enough practice maneuvering in water to
manipulate the natural buoyancy of her body, but either way she was
stuck in an L-position with her legs sticking straight out in front.
In addition to being physically fine she also seems not to have been
affected emotionally.  We were near more water today, wading in a
stream, and she didn't seem fearful:
I'm feeling very lucky that my aunt happened to see her in a risky
location and that I was able to get there in time, and I'm kicking
myself for conflating "shallow enough to stand" with "shallow enough
that a surprised and disoriented kid coming in at an awkward angle
will reliably be able to stand."

data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者如何用开源软件复活一台已有十年历史的Navman Bike 1000（实际为Mio Cyclo 200的贴牌产品）自行车导航设备。该设备因官方地图更新工具失效而无法获取新地图，但作者通过逆向工程，使用Windows CE 6.0和开源导航软件NaVeGIS，结合OpenStreetMap项目更新了地图。作者还提到该设备甚至可以运行游戏DOOM。文章批评了制造商通过计划报废促使消费者频繁购买新设备的做法，并建议厂商应开源旧设备的软件和硬件以减少电子垃圾。尽管设备已过时，但其硬件状态良好，电池续航达5小时，屏幕在户外清晰可见。作者对设备的功能表示满意，并希望厂商能提供付费地图更新服务。

Bringing a Decade Old Bicycle Navigator Back to Life with Open Source Software (and DOOM)
Published:
25-07-2025 23:37
| Author: Remy van Elst |
Text only version of this article
Table of Contents
Planned Obsolescence
Navman Bike 1000 / Mio Cyclo 200
First Impressions
mitmproxy & WireShark
Researching the firmware and DODGE.exe
Replacing DODGE.exe
NAVeGIS
Conclusion
I recently found a Navman Bike 1000 in a thrift store for EUR 10. This is a
bike computer, a navigation device for cyclists, made by MiTaC, the same
company that makes the Mio bike computers. This Navman Bike 1000 is a
rebadged
Mio Cyclo 200
. It's from 2015 and as you might have guessed, no more
map updates. There seem to be newer maps from 2020, but the official download
tool fails.
Planned Obsolescence at its best
. The device is still in very
good condition, the battery runs for 5 hours, the screen has great visibility
outside and the software is extensive.
NAVeGIS Open Source navigation with up to date maps
Recently I removed all Google Ads from this site due to their invasive tracking, as well as Google Analytics. Please, if you found this content useful, consider a small donation using any of the options below. It means the world to me if you  show your appreciation and you'll help pay the server costs:
GitHub Sponsorship
PCBWay referral link (You get $5, I get $20 after you've placed an order)
Digital Ocea referral link  ($200 credit for 60 days. Spend $25 after your credit expires and I'll get $25!)
This article shows how I dabbled a bit in reverse engineering, figuring out
the device runs Windows CE 6.0 and using Total Commander and
NaVeGIS
together with Open Street Map to
get up to date maps from the OpenFietsMap project, allowing me to use this
device for navigation with the most up to date maps. Since it is all open
source, even if the current map provider would stop, I can always make my own
maps.
Oh and it runs DOOM:
There is no other input than the touch screen, so I can shoot and nothing
more, but hey, it runs DOOM!
Planned Obsolescence
Mio
still makes newer devices like this one
,
which probably only last 2 years and then the maps are out of date with no
updates.
I'd even be willing to pay Mio for updated maps for this older model.
The original maps (kaarten, Dutch) are from 2015.
I wonder why a company would assign its engineers the task of providing maps
for old devices when newer gizmos consistently generate hundreds of dollars
every two years. The high prices of new Garmin units, for instance, make it
clear where their development priorities lie.
Why are there no laws requiring device manufacturers to
open source all software and hardware for consumer devices no longer sold?
This would not directly impact their revenue and would help reduce the
growing volume of e-waste. However, I believe such a measure would likely
shrink their profit margins, as consumers might no longer purchase new
devices annually if existing models remained functional for ten years.
You could turn this thought around. There is no information on the box nor in
the manual regarding (free) map updates, so you could expect nothing, no
updates at all. That they provided 5 years (2015 - 2020) of free map updates
is nice, but since it was never promised, we should not complain. The promise
was NO map updates, but you still got 5 years worth.
Navman Bike 1000 / Mio Cyclo 200
To start this post off here are some pictures of the device and a global
overview.
This is the unit with box:
Here is the Mio counterpart, mounted on a bike.
Both units are almost exactly the same except for housing colour and
background, software wise this article will work on both the Navman Bike 1000
and the Mio Cyclo 200.
Here is an excerpt from
its introduction in 2015
:
The Mio Cyclo 200 is an entry level bike navigation device with a 3.5-inch
color touchscreen and a very simple interface. It offers address
navigation, GPX track import, and a special "Surprise Me" feature that
creates random routes based on time or distance. It is loaded with
OpenStreetMap data for 23 Western European countries and includes
cycling-specific points of interest like repair shops and restaurants.
It is waterproof, designed for outdoor use, and has a battery life of around
10 hours. There's also a "Where am I" function to quickly check your
location. Mounting options include a handlebar mount, and a stem mount
(Garmin mount). Updates are handled via a desktop application. The device
focuses on basic navigation without training features, making it ideal for
leisure riders and e-bike users, with a price of EUR 179.99.
First Impressions
Mounting on the bike was very easy and the battery still holds charge up to 8
hours. It gets a GPS fix quite fast when you are outside. The software is
basic, but for its intended use case it's fine. You can enter an address or

data.title: Inverted Indexes: A Step-by-Step Implementation Guide (2023)
data.author: klaussilveira
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了倒排索引的概念及其在文档搜索系统中的应用。倒排索引通过将单词作为键，文档ID作为值，使得根据关键词快速查找文档成为可能。文章举例说明了如何构建简单的倒排索引，例如给定一些句子，生成如下索引：`{"hobbit": [1, 3], "television": [2], ...}`。这种结构支持高效的查询操作，如AND、OR、NOT等逻辑查询。

文章还详细描述了如何实现一个基础的倒排索引类，包括添加单词和查找文档的方法。接着，介绍了`IndexGenerator`类，它负责读取文件、分词、清理数据（如去除停用词和无用字符），并将单词添加到索引中。

总的来说，倒排索引是实现高效文档搜索的基础，本文提供了一个简单的实现示例，并提到在实际应用中可进一步优化，如增加相关性排序和词干提取等功能。

Search
Before we start with the implementation, let's talk about why would you actually need an inverted index in a real life.
Why would anyone need inverted index at all
Imagine you need to create a system that would quickly look up a document, given several words from it - something like a wiki search. Simplest option I can think of would be to scan through each document, marking ones that have all the necessary words. That might work at first, but such solution wouldn't scale, as each new document increases time to answer any query.
Can we do something better? Actually, we can! If user wants to search by words - then words should be keys in our "database" (index). What would the values be in that case? Document ids, or any other unique references / pointers, that contain this word.
How inverted indexes work
Imagine we have documents like:
id: 1; Text: “In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit.”
id: 2; Text: “The sky above the port was the color of television, tuned to a dead channel.”
id: 3; Text: "Hobbits Are Amazing Creatures"
In this case, our index would look something like that:
{
"hobbit": [1, 3],
"television": [2],
"hole": [1],
...
}
Seems quite obvious how we got here, right?
Now if user queries system for "hobbit" - we look up this key (in O(1) time), and return document 1 and 3.
This structure also solves case when we need to do queries like NOT, AND and OR - we get sets of documents by each key, and then do usual set operations, like intersect in case of AND, or diff in case of NOT. Hence for query like "hobbit AND hole" we will look up sets [1, 3] and [1], their intersection would be [1], and we would return document with id=1.
Obviously all this is just a tip of the iceberg, the most naive implementation - real-word document indexing / querying systems could rank results based on relevance, do different sorts of fuzzy search, faceted search etc, but still, naive implementation is a great place to start.
So - let's start, and implement it.
Implementation
I would start somewhat "from the bottom" - so we'll first implement just class representing Inverted Index, with ability to add and lookup token there, then add some helpers to index full documents, and then provide the scaffolding that allows to actually run this as an application.
So, let's start with class representing InvertedIndex itself:

Token
= String
type
Filename
= String

tokenIndex: Map[
Token
, Set[
Filename
]] = HashMap[
Token
, Set[
Filename
]]()
)
As I mentioned in the beginning of the article, our index itself would be powered by a usual
Map[String, Set[String]]
- mapping from indexed word to a list of document ids (or, in our case, just document names).
Not much going on just yet - let's do something useful, at least add a method to add word to the index, and get added documents afterwards:

add

Token

Filename
): InvertedIndex = {
tokenIndex.get(token)
match
{
case
Some(set) =>
// we already know this token - add filename to the set
InvertedIndex(tokenIndex.updated(token, set + filename))
case
None =>
// token didn't previously exist - creating new set
InvertedIndex(tokenIndex.updated(token, Set(filename)))
}
}
def
getDocumentsForToken
(token:
Token
): Set[
Filename
] =
tokenIndex.getOrElse(token, Set.
empty
[String])
Not a lot is going on here, but our inverted index is already usable!
Though we still need something to add words into the index. We'll create
IndexGenerator
class for that purpose:
class
IndexGenerator(filesToIndex: List[String]) {
def
generateIndex
(): InvertedIndex = {
logger
.info(
"Indexer started"
)
filesToIndex
.map(
readFile
)
.foldLeft(InvertedIndex()) {
case
(idx, doc) =>
val
updIdx = processDocument(idx, doc)
updIdx
}
}
private def
processDocument
(index: InvertedIndex, document: GenericDocument): InvertedIndex =
document.text
.split(
" "
)
.flatMap(processToken)
.foldLeft(index)(_.add(_, document.fileName))
private def
processToken
(token: String): Option[String] = {
val
tokenLower = token.toLowerCase
if
(tokenLower.isEmpty ||
StringUtils.
getStopWords
.contains(tokenLower)) {
None
}
else
{
Some(tokenLower.removeTags().removeNumbers())
}
}
}
So what do we have here?
IndexGenerator takes a list of files to index, reads them from disk, and "processes". processing is just splitting whole text into words (or "tokens"), a little bit of cleanup via processToken function, and adding them one by one to the InvertedIndex.
I won't get into details of StringUtils functions here - their implementation is quite obvious from names and in any real-life application you would actually spend some time coming up with good data cleanup rules. One thing to mention is stop words - those are basically all the words that you often encounter in any text, but are not very helpful in actual search - words like
the
,
a
,
and
etc. You'll also probably want to do some stemming / lemmatization, so that documents with word "democratical" could be found via "democracy" query.
44658665.article_summary:
本文介绍了倒排索引的概念及其在文档搜索系统中的应用。倒排索引通过将单词作为键，文档ID作为值，使得根据关键词快速查找文档成为可能。文章举例说明了如何构建简单的倒排索引，例如给定一些句子，生成如下索引：`{"hobbit": [1, 3], "television": [2], ...}`。这种结构支持高效的查询操作，如AND、OR、NOT等逻辑查询。

文章还详细描述了如何实现一个基础的倒排索引类，包括添加单词和查找文档的方法。接着，介绍了`IndexGenerator`类，它负责读取文件、分词、清理数据（如去除停用词和无用字符），并将单词添加到索引中。

总的来说，倒排索引是实现高效文档搜索的基础，本文提供了一个简单的实现示例，并提到在实际应用中可进一步优化，如增加相关性排序和词干提取等功能。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在红蓝队模型中的应用及其在不同领域的类比和实际效果

不同观点：
• **ants_everywhere** 认为红蓝队模型在AI中是有用的。蓝队负责头脑风暴，而红队负责检验和挑战。他还指出，安全系统的强弱不仅仅取决于最薄弱的环节，还与多层防御机制有关。
• **_alternator_** 表示红蓝队模型有助于理解LLM（大型语言模型）的当前实用性。他认为LLM在添加测试方面较为可靠，但在修复错误或添加功能时容易出现问题，例如编写非健壮的代码。
• **nostrademons** 将红蓝队模型类比于商业领域，指出蓝队行业（如电力、银行）是经济的基础，而红队行业（如餐饮、旅游）则提升消费者福利。他认为，从经济角度看，成为蓝队一员更有优势，尽管技术本身可能在红队中更实用。
• **javier_e06** 认为红蓝队模型在网络安全中是两个对等的 forces，但在软件开发中并不完全适用。测试本身也是代码，可能会存在bug，因此测试也需要被测试。
• **ashton314** 提到RSA算法的创建过程类似于红蓝队模型，其中Rivest和Shamir提出想法，Adleman负责找出安全漏洞。
• **recipe19** 指出，将防御仅视为最薄弱环节的观点是危险和天真的。多层防御是必要的，因为任何单一层次都无法达到100%的安全性。
• **TheGRS** 认为，AI模型应同时参与红蓝队角色，并应参与管理任务，使开发者更像监督者。
• **scoreandmore** 分享了使用Claude分析网站安全性的经验，发现其建议较为表面，并质疑是否通过攻击网站能获得更深入的改进建议。
• **zkmon** 提出，红队不应仅仅是一个团队，而是背景环境的一部分，通过与前景的互动和适应来实现进化。
• **jedberg** 指出，混沌工程是为了在操作中充当“红队”，通过探索所有可能的失败空间来提前发现问题。
• **bodhi_mind** 询问是否存在同时承担红蓝队角色的“紫队”，以及这是否会破坏两者的目的。
• **1970-01-01** 认为使用进攻和防御来描述红蓝队可能更直观，并质疑为何Terry Tao未使用这些术语。
• **LeifCarrotson** 强调红队的重要性，尤其是在不可靠和不透明的AI工具背景下，但指出一些企业为了短期利润可能选择忽视测试和安全。
• **hiq** 询问LLM是否能在形式化证明中发挥“蓝队”角色，帮助数学家节省时间并专注于更困难的部分。

补充讨论：
• 技术细节如JWTs的生命周期和网站安全性改进建议（scoreandmore）。
• 对网站字体可读性的技术问题反馈（Fabricio20）。

争议焦点：
• 红蓝队模型在不同领域的适用性和类比的准确性。
• AI工具在红蓝队模型中的实际效果和可靠性，尤其是在测试和安全方面的应用。

data.title: Copyparty – Turn almost any device into a file server
data.author: saint11
data.article_summary: **Copyparty** 是一个便携式文件服务器，支持可恢复的上传/下载，具有去重、WebDAV、FTP、TFTP、媒体索引、缩略图等功能。它仅需Python（2或3）运行，所有依赖项均为可选。支持多种协议如HTTP、WebDAV、FTP、TFTP、SMB/CIFS，并提供Android应用和iPhone快捷方式。主要功能包括文件上传/下载、文件搜索、批量重命名、RSS监控、媒体播放、播放列表创建、文本和Markdown文件查看等。此外，它支持Zeroconf、mDNS和SSDP等网络发现协议，允许通过QR码快速访问。用户可通过命令行或配置文件自定义服务器设置，并可启用文件去重和索引功能。

data.title: The Geological Sublime
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary: Lewis Hyde's essay "The Geological Sublime" explores the intersection of deep geological time, climate change, and human history. He reflects on the awe-inspiring power of earthquakes and other geological events that reveal the immense scales of time, citing Charles Lyell and Darwin's observations of Earth's transformative forces. Hyde contrasts these ancient processes with current rapid climate changes, such as ocean acidification, which are occurring on much shorter timescales. He connects his scientific interests to personal experiences, particularly his enjoyment of observing butterflies, which grounds his understanding of nature's wonders and vulnerabilities in the present day. The essay underscores the tension between the slow pace of geological change and the accelerated impacts of human-driven climate shifts.

Butterflies, deep time, and climate change

It is not inadmissible to think of an epoch
Â . . .
not too far distant, when humanity, to ensure its survival, will find itself reduced to desisting from any further âmakingâ of history.
âMircea Eliade
T
he earthquake shook us awake at 4:31 in the morning. We hurried into a closet while, for fifteen seconds, it finished its business and the car alarms down on Third and California began their complaint. When we emerged, the night sky greeted us through a crack in the wall and chunks of plaster sat smack on the Apple keyboard. The cat had fled.
Out on the street, the hanging dust of rendered Sheetrock mixed with the scent of potted plants and, for those of us standing in our nightclothes, a dose of adrenaline improved the sense of awe. Suddenly the inhuman forces of the raw earth had struck us, forces that lift mountains and sink cities. And suddenly there was a rip in time, a twenty-heartbeat glimpse into the equally inhuman roll of ages where continents join and break apart.
Thirty miles north of our Santa Monica apartment, Oat Mountain had risen fifteen inches and moved six inches to one side. That mountain sits in southern Californiaâs Transverse Ranges, which began their rise from the sea about 5Â million years ago, having first been caught, some 15Â million years earlier, between tectonic plates that spun them clockwise so they now sit at right angles to the coast. The geology of the Transverse Ranges consists largely of granite from the Mesozoic Eraâ66Â to 252Â million years agoâwith some even earlier Precambrian material, at least 1.6Â billion years old.
These are large numbers. They belong to the calculus of deep time as introduced to the world by British scientists in the mid-nineteenth centuryânamely, the preeminent geologist of the age, Charles Lyell, and Charles Darwin, who borrowed Lyellâs unbounded temporality and used it to underpin his theory of evolution.
Long before he formulated that theory, Darwin himself had witnessed what he called âthe forces which slowly and by little starts uplift continents.â The year was 1835 and Darwin was near
ing the end of a five-year journey around the world aboard the British surveying ship
the HMSÂ
Beagle.
In Chile, he was onshore one February day taking a nap when the ground began to rock. The quake lasted two minutes; its only local effect was to make Darwin âalmost giddy.â
Nearly two weeks later, he arrived in ConcepciÃ³n to find a completely ruined city. After offering an inventory of all that was lost, Darwin, ever the student geologist, noted that âthe land round the Bay of Concepcion was upraised two or three feetâ and that on the nearby island of Santa MarÃ­a they found âmussel-shells
still adhering to the rocks,
ten feet above high-water mark.â Later that month, Darwin climbed high into the Andes, where he found âshells which were once crawling on the bottom of the sea, now standing nearly 14,000 feet above its level.â It had taken about twenty-five million years for those shells to reach that height.
For several years now, I have been reading these early theorists, thinking that their vision of geological and evolutionary time might give me a context for understanding not just the age of mountains but something more current. Itâs one thing to hear of the millions of years it took the Andes to rise; itâs quite another to hear that, in mere centuries, the oceans may reach levels of acidity not seen in 300 million years, or that the earth is the hottest it has been in the past 125,000 years. These days, geological forces, formerly the stuff of earthquakes and volcanoes, have escaped the confines of deep time to present themselves daily, winter, spring, summer, and fall.
It is on this other end of the scale of timeâin seasons rather than eonsâthat my own interest in natural science began and where today it finds its focus and concern. As a child and to this day, one of my deepest pleasures has come from walking farm fields and alpine meadows, watching for butterflies, a pursuit that takes on a formal touch each year when, in early July, I join the annual Concord, Massachusetts, butterfly count. Fifteen or twenty naturalists, most of us amateurs, gather and split into several teams to search a set list of local fields and woods. data.title: Getting the KIM-1 to talk to my Mac
data.author: jgrahamc
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何让1976年的KIM-1计算机通过电流环接口与终端（如Teletype）通信，避免直接使用其键盘和小显示屏的麻烦。KIM-1使用20mA电流环，而非常见的RS-232电压接口。作者利用一个RS-232到电流环的适配器套件，通过修改使其与KIM-1兼容，解决了接收端没有电流回路的问题。具体修改包括将一个光隔离器的引脚与KIM-1连接，而非接地。最终，作者成功通过USB适配器和终端软件与KIM-1实现通信，并能以300波特率运行，甚至模拟打孔纸带格式上传程序。这使老旧硬件重新焕发活力。

44684055.article_content:
I've written before about
my 1976 KIM-1
and
code I wrote
for a similar one long ago. But I hadn't done much with the KIM-1 and strongly believe that old hardware need to be living machines not still lives. But using the KIM-1 directly (via its keypad and little hexadecimal display) is painful. I wanted to be able to use it with a terminal.
Luckily, the KIM-1 was designed to interface to a terminal: a
Model 33 ASR Teletype
. Teletypes use a type of interface which is unusual to most people (unless you work with industrial machinery where it's pretty common). That interface is a
current loop
.
A current loop uses current (often 20mA) rather than voltage (such as the voltage levels seen in common serial interfaces). Prior to the creation of
RS-232
, current loops were very common. Current loops are still used in industrial settings partly because they have good noise immunity, can go for long distances, and are simple and reliable.
In the KIM-1 manual there's a picture of the way its current loop works when connected to a Teletype:
When the KIM-1 wants to send data to the Teletype it uses pins S and U of one of its edge connectors. S is permanently connected to +5V via a 150 ohm resistor. When the KIM-1 receives data from the Teletype's keyboard it uses pins R and T. Just like S, R is permanently connected to +5V. The important thing to note is that the KIM-1 is responsible for the current: the Teletype is entirely "dumb". This will matter later in this blog post.
I happened to have lying around
a kit to make an adapter between RS-232 and the Siemens SIMATIC S5 current loop
.
A simple kit to build. Since USB to RS-232 adapters are easy to find I'd be able to communicate with the KIM-1 using it. But first check the circuit diagram of this adapter. There's a small problem on the receive side.
As is pretty common with current loop applications, optoisolators are used. OK1 handles when the device connected to the RS-232 transmits something. And you can see from the diagram, it expects to be getting 5V, 20mA in on its pin 5 and then out again on pin 4. So, that'll work perfectly for the "keyboard" connection to the KIM-1 (pins R and T).
But the receive side is a different story. It's handled by OK2 and it's expecting 5V, 20mA on pin 1, but pin 2 goes to GND. So, there's no "loop" back to the device. This won't work with the KIM-1 without a small modification.
I built the kit and and tested it against the KIM-1 like this:
Looks messy but it validated the little modification I needed to make and that I could talk to the KIM-1. Here it is talking at 300 baud using the RS-232 to USB adapter seen above.
So, what's the modification? Well, pin 2 of OK2 goes to ground and we don't want it to, we want it to go the KIM-1's pin U. There are two ways to do this. I could have cut the track on the back of the board that goes from pin 2 to ground, and soldered a wire on the back.
But this kit came with all the chips socketed so I took an even simpler route. Bend pin 2 away from the socket and solder directly to it.
And that worked fine. The kit also came with a nice little box and so the final adapter looks neat.
The grey wire goes to the KIM-1, the white wire is a USB-A cable that I'm using to power the adapter and the KIM-1 itself.
The KIM-1 will happily communicate as 1200 baud with 7 bit ASCII and 2 stop bits. I'm using minicom to communicate with it. The main thing is to set the delete key to send DEL instead of BS since the KIM-1 needs to receive a DEL on start up so that it can measure the Mac's transmission speed.
One of the Teletype functions available is to load a program from punched tape. I don't have an actual Teletype but I can emulate the punched tape format and that'll allow me to upload programs easily.
The format itself is not complicated.

data.title: Viral Language
data.author: lermontov
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对年轻人（尤其是Z世代）使用语言现象的看法，以及语言演变的历史背景和相关概念的辨析。

不同观点：
• [kazinator] 认为诸如 "aura"（气场）和 "brain rot"（脑残）等词汇并非新创，并提供了词源证据。例如，"aura" 一词早在1732年就有使用记录，而 "brain-rot" 甚至可以追溯到1854年亨利·梭罗的作品《瓦尔登湖》。这一观点强调了这些词汇的历史渊源，暗示它们在现代被认为是新词可能是一种误解。

• [henriquegodoy] 强调语言和行为之间的相互影响，认为行为会影响语言，而语言反过来又会影响行为，形成一种循环。这种观点关注语言演变的动态过程，强调社会行为对语言创新的推动作用。

• [bitwize] 提出需要区分几种不同的语言现象：Z世代的俚语（如 "rizz"）、为避免被平台惩罚而使用的代用语（如 "unalive" 代表 "kill"），以及用星号替代字母以避免提及某些不受欢迎的人物（如 "El*n M*sk"）。此外，bitwize 质疑一些被认为是Z世代使用的词汇（如 "cheugy"）的真实性，认为这些词汇可能是媒体和市场营销人员虚构并传播的，类似于1990年代“垃圾摇滚俚语”的骗局。

补充讨论：

data.author: jsnider3
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在社会中的影响，尤其是关于信息可信性和操控的问题，以及AI技术普及后的潜在后果。

不同观点：
• [jerf] 认为，随着高度说服性AI的普及，人们将难以信任任何信息来源。他担心未来社会将充满定制的、具有说服性的内容，导致人们无法再获取可信的信息。他提出了一个问题：当信息环境充斥着试图操控我们的内容时，人们如何能做出明智的决策？最终，获取信息可能会变得弊大于利。
  
• [ianbicking] 则认为，虽然很多AI公司目前关注于最大化用户参与度，但AI技术是开放的，任何人都可以创建不以盈利最大化为目标的AI应用。他反驳了将所有AI公司视为追求相同目标的固定实体的观点，强调技术开放性带来的多样化可能性。

• [amradio1989] 表达了对人类依赖AI作为陪伴的反对意见，认为只有人类才能成为合适的 companions。他暗示了某些权力机构可能不愿意传播这一观点，暗示了某种潜在的利益冲突。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI技术对信息环境的影响以及人类如何应对潜在的信任危机。Jerf预见了信息不可信的未来，而ianbicking则关注于AI技术的开放性所带来的不同发展路径。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是人类与AI之间的关系，amradio1989明确反对AI作为人类伴侣的角色，提出了对AI在人类生活中角色的伦理思考。

• Jerf还提到了历史上的类似现象（如1950年代的广告），说明社会需要不断发展防御机制以应对新的说服手段，这暗示了当前和未来应对策略的重要性。

data.title: A Photonic SRAM with Embedded XOR Logic for Ultra-Fast In-Memory Computing
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种新型的光子静态随机存取存储器（pSRAM）单元，称为X-pSRAM，它集成了XOR逻辑功能，用于超快速的存储内计算。该设计通过交叉耦合微环谐振器和差分光电二极管，实现了在光域内以至少10 GHz的速度进行读、写和计算操作。利用波分复用技术，X-pSRAM可以在单次操作中完成n位XOR计算，支持大规模并行处理，显著降低计算延迟和能耗。在GlobalFoundries的45SPCLO节点上验证表明，X-pSRAM在XOR计算中每比特能耗为13.2 fJ，适用于加密、高维计算和神经网络等领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ASIC性能、内存计算的应用场景、DARPA资助背景、TCAM面积问题及其应用领域

不同观点：
• **mikewarot**：认为基于当前的3nm工艺，可以制造出时钟频率超过10 GHz的非冯·诺依曼架构计算引擎，而无需借助光子学。他强调通过避免使用RAM，直接处理数据流可以实现显著性能提升。给出的例子是使用老旧的Skywater 130 nm工艺制造2.5+ GHz振荡器，并推测更先进工艺的潜力。

• **Scene_Cast2**：对内存计算的应用场景感到困惑，质疑其在主流和 niche 应用中的定位。他提出了关于内存计算在实际应用中的具体用例问题，比如是否能有效处理矩阵乘法或前馈神经网络的偏置项，以及是否能用于常规业务逻辑的加速。他还将这种方法类比为更高效但可能功能有限的DSP或固定功能加速器。

• **inasio**：提到该技术源于DARPA资助的项目，并通过谷歌搜索验证资助的真实性，但未找到直接关联。

• **rapatel0**：关注TCAM（三态内容地址able存储器）的面积问题，认为0.1 mm^2的面积过大，可能成为项目推进的障碍，但同时认为如果能在服务器基础设施中应用或缩小面积，该技术仍有潜力。

• **latchkey**：认为该技术可能不会用于传统计算，而更可能应用于网络交换机或收发器中，以提高速度和降低功耗。

Title:
X-pSRAM: A Photonic SRAM with Embedded XOR Logic for Ultra-Fast In-Memory Computing
Authors:
Md Abdullah-Al Kaiser
,
Sugeet Sunder
,
Ajey P. Jacob
,
Akhilesh R. Jaiswal
View a PDF of the paper titled X-pSRAM: A Photonic SRAM with Embedded XOR Logic for Ultra-Fast In-Memory Computing, by Md Abdullah-Al Kaiser and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Traditional von Neumann architectures suffer from fundamental bottlenecks due to continuous data movement between memory and processing units, a challenge that worsens with technology scaling as electrical interconnect delays become more significant. These limitations impede the performance and energy efficiency required for modern data-intensive applications. In contrast, photonic in-memory computing presents a promising alternative by harnessing the advantages of light, enabling ultra-fast data propagation without length-dependent impedance, thereby significantly reducing computational latency and energy consumption. This work proposes a novel differential photonic static random access memory (pSRAM) bitcell that facilitates electro-optic data storage while enabling ultra-fast in-memory Boolean XOR computation. By employing cross-coupled microring resonators and differential photodiodes, the XOR-augmented pSRAM (X-pSRAM) bitcell achieves at least 10 GHz read, write, and compute operations entirely in the optical domain. Additionally, wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) enables n-bit XOR computation in a single-shot operation, supporting massively parallel processing and enhanced computational efficiency. Validated on GlobalFoundries' 45SPCLO node, the X-pSRAM consumed 13.2 fJ energy per bit for XOR computation, representing a significant advancement toward next-generation optical computing with applications in cryptography, hyperdimensional computing, and neural networks.

data.title: The 1970s psychology experiment behind 'Star Wars' special effects (2023)
data.author: cainxinth
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了20世纪70年代加州大学伯克利分校的一个心理学实验如何意外影响了《星球大战》等电影的特效制作。该实验由美国国家科学基金会资助，旨在通过微缩模型和计算机控制相机模拟逼真的社区环境。实验的核心成员John Dykstra、Jerry Jeffress和Alvah Miller后来成为乔治·卢卡斯创办的特效公司Industrial Light & Magic（ILM）的创始成员。他们基于实验开发的Dykstraflex系统 revolution 化了电影制作，尤其是在《星球大战》中的应用，创造了令人难忘的特效场景。该实验不仅推动了电影特效的发展，还为环境心理学领域的研究提供了新的方法，帮助改善城市规划和设计中的模拟技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同类型的模型和模拟系统在历史上的应用及其技术挑战

不同观点：
• **wanderingmoose**：提到20世纪80年代在Wright-Patterson空军基地看到的一个用于飞行模拟器的垂直安装的模型，模型细节令人惊叹。尽管该系统当时已不再使用，但通过摄像机在电视屏幕上呈现的效果非常逼真，模拟出真实的飞行体验。

• **kenjackson**：对1972年一段通过潜望镜驾驶穿过城市街道的影像表示印象深刻，认为模型的质感在视频中比早期模型制作时的效果要好，误以为最初看到的是真实街道。

• **sliken**：指出使用微缩模型和摄像机拍摄并制作特效镜头时存在时间消耗问题，拍摄和结果查看可能需要数天时间，且最终效果不一定理想。为解决这一问题，他们使用了三河计算机公司（后更名为PERQ Systems Corporation）的矢量显示器，实现实时预览，从而大幅提高工作效率。

• **drewcoo**：提供了一个HBO城市飞越插曲的链接，作为相关讨论的补充材料。

• **empath75**：认为这种模型技术是1972年工作的延续，但加入了计算机控制，而在1968年的《2001太空漫游》中，所有效果都是通过机械控制实现的。

补充讨论：
• 技术演进：从机械控制（2001太空漫游）到计算机控制（城市模型模拟）的转变，展示了技术在模型制作和模拟中的进步。
• 实时预览的重要性：sliken提到的矢量显示器显著提高了模型拍摄和特效制作的效率，解决了传统方法中反馈周期长的问题。

The 1970s psychology experiment behind 'Star Wars' special effects
Creating realistic simulations of neighborhoods using miniatures and computer-controlled cameras was the goal of an ambitious experiment designed by two NSF-funded researchers. What they didn't know was that their lab's research would influence how special effects are made in some of the most memorable movies and TV shows in history, from the first "Star Wars" movie to "The Mandalorian."
By Jason Stoughton
May 4, 2023
With mouths agape, movie audiences for more than 40 years have watched a certain outgunned rebel spaceship's futile attempt to flee a ginormous imperial star destroyer. That iconic opening shot of 1977's "Star Wars" is seared into the collective memory of millions, if not billions, of people. It was, of course, an elaborate fake — constructed and photographed by skilled artists in a humble warehouse outside Los Angeles. Far, far away from the Galactic Empire.
That scene and many others were created for the first "Star Wars" movie by Industrial Light & Magic, George Lucas' then-fledgling special effects company. The staff of ILM ignited a revolution in filmmaking aesthetics. They combined technology and artistry with a keen understanding of the fundamentals of human perception. That innovative fusion was based on experimental techniques first tested in a research project at the University of California, Berkeley and supported by the U.S. National Science Foundation.
"The focus of the project required that I figure out, in a scientific way, the things that made the image believable," says John Dykstra, who worked on the experiment in Berkeley's Environmental Simulation Laboratory in the 1970s along with Jerry Jeffress and Alvah Miller. A few years later, all three would become founding members of ILM, where they would expand on the work at Berkeley to create a computer-controlled camera system capable of movie-quality special effects — the eponymous "Dykstraflex" system which was first used for "Star Wars."
Credit: Courtesy of Lucasfilm Ltd. Copyright Industrial Light & Magic © & ™ Lucasfilm Ltd. All rights reserved.
The Dykstraflex system, including the crane and dolly track, with a model TIE fighter and bluescreen background.
The research and technological innovations achieved in the Berkeley lab provided a new understanding of how people respond to what they see — be it real or on celluloid — and how that understanding could be applied. In the process, Dykstra and others in the lab prototyped some of the techniques and equipment that the inventive team at ILM would later use to draw audiences into a perceptually believable fantasy with dogfighting TIE fighters and trench-running X-wings.
"The one that blew everyone away was that very first shot in Star Wars with this ship that looks like it's a mile long, flying overhead," remembers ILM Executive Creative Director John Knoll of his reaction when he first saw "Star Wars" as a boy.
"And to discover that it's a 3-foot-long model? It's just, how did they do it?"
A new hope... for public planning
Donald Appleyard was a professor of urban design at UC Berkeley with a passion for how streets, neighborhoods and entire cities can be designed to maximize the quality of life and safety of their residents. In the early 1970s he partnered with his friend, Berkeley psychologist Kenneth Craik, and together they helped establish the new field of environmental psychology, which investigates how people are affected by their surrounding environment, from busy streets to peaceful parks.
In 1970, then-President Richard Nixon signed the "National Environmental Policy Act" into law, which required federal agencies to start taking into account the environmental impacts of construction projects, like highways. The purpose of the law was to prevent environmental damage and to "stimulate the health and welfare of man."
The new law spurred Appleyard and Craik to tackle a thorny issue in the planning and development of public works, says urban designer Peter Bosselmann, who worked with Appleyard and Craik in UC Berkeley's Environmental Simulation Laboratory and later led the lab after Appleyard's death in 1982.
The problem was that simulations of construction projects, like static models and drawings, don't always accurately convey how the project will ultimately be perceived by the people who might eventually inhabit them or live nearby.
"Drawings and perspectives are necessarily selective, and planners choose the viewpoints and features that best communicate their ideas of what the project ought to be like," wrote Appleyard in 1977 in
Berkeley Environmental Simulation Laboratory: A Tool for Transportation
. "At best, there is a rich mixture of hope in these presentations; at worst there is downright deception."

data.article_summary: 文章批评了Windows 11操作系统中充斥的各种干扰性功能和广告，称其环境如同一个充满微攻击的雷区，影响了用户的工作效率。作者将这种侵入性软件比作恶意软件，指出这些功能不断监控和干扰用户操作。尽管目前有一些工具可以清理和优化Windows系统，但它们往往不够直观或可靠，且更新不及时。文章呼吁开发一种自动化、可信赖且易用的Windows清理工具，以对抗系统中的不良功能。这种工具应开源、专业，并能不断更新以应对新问题，最终帮助用户重获工作效率，同时挑战微软的垄断地位。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows操作系统的使用体验及其替代方案

不同观点：

44710965.article_content:
OSes
13
Windows 11 is a minefield of micro-aggressions in the shipping lane of progress
13
A better minesweeper is needed. Time for an intervention to save Microsoft from itself
Rupert Goodwins
Mon 28 Jul 2025
//
13:45 UTC
Workflow. Productivity. Enablement. These are the holy words by which software companies sanctify their ever more plunder-hungry Viking raids on enterprise IT coffers. If only they were true. At least Vikings didn’t pretend to be offering monastery renovations and smart haircuts when they turned up.
Microsoft, sad to say, is at it like gangbusters. So desperate is Redmond for your attention as a path to monetization, it has made the Windows 11 environment an ADHD horror show, full of distractions, promotions and snares. You can, with some work,
rewire things
behind the scenes to get rid of a lot of these, at least until things get quietly restored or re-enabled.
If you're forced to use Windows 11, here's how to steal some of your time back
READ MORE
Then there’s the heavy artillery of AI, a relentless barrage of features and functions that just want to be your friend. You know, the sort of friend who wants to
constantly video what you’re doing and send it back to Mother
. But not in a creepy way, you understand. Promise.
There is a word for intrusive, unwanted software that intervenes in your work to advertise or engage you in unwanted interaction. The same word describes software that constantly monitors and exfiltrates what’s going on between you and your data. That word is malware, and by now it’s clear that for Windows it isn’t a class of third-party nasties, it’s an edition name. The attacks are coming from inside the code.
This provides refreshing clarity. The industry as a whole hasn’t done a great job at closing down malware, but it’s a known enemy that’s been with us since the 1980s. We know how to deal with it, at least in theory. We know that to be effective, anti-malware software has to be trustworthy, adaptive to a changing threat landscape, unintrusive, and capable of being successfully used by people with a wide range of technical skills.
What we have at the moment falls far short of this. There are numerous Windows de-bloaters and clean-up tools, but there are also plenty of pop-ups and other dodgy productions that fly that false flag to slip in a payload. The most trustworthy mechanism to get the good stuff is GitHub. That's great if you're in the tech priesthood, intimidatingly weird if you're not.
Doing things manually by recipe is also less than optimal. If it involves tweaking the registry, you don't want Arnold from Accounts chancing their arm. Plus, how-to guides suffer from the same accelerated obsolescence as any other specific technical advice online. The text is static, the target changes.
The ideal, therefore, is an automated Windows detoxifier with a solid chain of trust; one that's rapidly updated to track new outbreaks of unwholesomeness; one that's constructed to be usable by anyone, and to be configurable so that the user can dial in what they want to go.
The reason for this level of slick presentation is because the ultimate goal is to make Windows a place for workflow, productivity and enablement – again, not just because of the software, but permanently. There has to be a war of attrition, and it's one we must win. Effort spent by Microsoft to annoy, patronize and distract us must be wasted, and seen by Microsoft to be wasted.
Thus, the software must be fit for consumers and enterprise. It has to be open source, and it has to look professional. It can and obviously should bring together existing examples of good Windows detox tools as there's a lot of work and expertise there, making them seamless parts of the package.
While this is within the capabilities of many open source package developers, and there are plausible paths to making money through tiered enterprise licensing through support customization and automation, the whole thing would fit best under an existing and trusted open source name, a distro, application or utility package that is already in widespread use.
The tiny tech tribe who could change the world tomorrow but won't
When even Microsoft can't understand its own Outlook, big tech is stuck in a swamp of its own making
Windows isn't an OS, it's a bad habit that wants to become an addiction
Microsoft tastes the unexpected consequences of tariffs on time
It seems perverse for someone like Ubuntu to offer a package that seemingly negates one of the biggest advantages of the Linux desktop, that it doesn't try to steal your soul. Why waste time and effort helping the opposition? But think of it more in terms of getting FOSS into the very center of the unassailable fortress of Windows enterprise IT dominance. Think of it as a live, ongoing demonstration of FOSS principles of user-centered computing. Think how much it would annoy Redmond.
Windows has long been suffering from auto-malware-ification, and we need a cure. That cure will only come

data.author: nsagheen
data.article_summary: 文章描述了在裁员潮中幸存的员工面临的困境。虽然保住了工作，但他们感到内疚和压力，因为办公室变得冷清，工作量却增加。微软等公司的大规模裁员让留下来的员工不得不面对更大的工作负担和心理压力。文章指出，这些员工不仅要承受额外的工作，还要应对幸存者内疚感，同时公司的短期利润导向让长期创新变得更加困难。这种局面不仅影响个人心理健康，还波及家庭生活，反映了企业贪婪对员工的深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕技术行业内各种现象的讨论，包括企业裁员、技术转型、开发策略、企业文化等问题。

不同观点：
• 一些文章（如"Surviving the Cut, but Drowning in Tasks"）讨论了在裁员潮中幸存下来的员工，虽然保住了工作，但面临工作负担加重和心理压力的双重挑战。文章指出这种“裁员彩票”的苦涩结果，即留下来的员工并不一定好过。

• 另一篇文章（"The Great Divide: High Octane vs. Lackadaisical Laggards in IT"）提到了IT行业中高效员工与懒散员工之间的巨大差距，认为这种分化会对团队合作和整体效率产生负面影响。

• 关于技术转型的讨论（如"Southwest's Turbulent Transition"和"The Algorithmic Renaissance"）中，有观点认为企业在技术变革中面临挑战，但同时也有机会通过正确实施人工智能等新技术获得优势。

• "Bludgeoned Buzzwords"系列文章批评了在企业中滥用流行术语（如“云优先”、“ lift and shift”）的现象，认为这些术语往往掩盖了实际执行中的复杂性和困难。

• 关于企业贪婪的讨论（如"Corporate Greed Chronicles"系列），一些文章揭露了大公司通过裁员、削减成本来追求利润最大化，同时忽视员工福利和社会责任的问题。

• 对于DevOps的讨论（"DevOps in the Crosshairs"），有人质疑DevOps是否被过度炒作，其实际价值是否与其宣传相符。

补充讨论：
• 一些文章讨论了具体的技术工具和平台，如C#、Microsoft D365FO等，分析了它们的优缺点以及在实际应用中的挑战。

• 关于企业文化的讨论（如"DEI Theater of Corporate America"和"The IT Monoculture Mirage"），提出了企业在多样性与包容性（DEI）政策上的形式主义问题，以及所谓“最佳实践”是否真的最佳的质疑。

• 最后，关于领导力和管理策略的讨论（如"Fractional Leadership in IT"和"High-Agency Playbook"），提出了在IT部门中如何有效实施领导力，以及如何打破供应商锁定，实现自主创新的问题。

争议焦点：
• 企业裁员策略及其对员工的影响是争议的核心之一，一部分人认为裁员是企业生存的必要手段，另一部分人则认为这是企业贪婪和短视的表现，忽视了员工的长期利益。

• 技术转型中的实际效果也是争议点，一些人看好新技术（如AI）的潜力，另一些人则认为这些技术被过度炒作，实际效果有限。

magine waking up to a job you once loved, only to find the office feels like a ghost town. Your inbox is heavier, your to-do list longer, and the desk next to you, once occupied by a colleague who shared your coffee runs and code reviews, is now a stark reminder of the latest round of layoffs. As an IT professional at a firm specializing in software development, ERP advisory, data science, organizational effectiveness, or developer advocacy, you’re among the “lucky” ones who survived the cut. But the celebration is short-lived, the aftermath of layoffs, as seen in cases like
Microsoft’s 15,000 job cuts
over recent months, paints a grim picture for those left behind. You’re expected to show up with the same enthusiasm, the same hunger to innovate, as if the rug wasn’t just pulled out from under your peers’ livelihoods. The toll on mental health and family life is real, and it’s not just a personal struggle, it’s a systemic failure driven by corporate greed that prioritizes short-term profits over long-term innovation.
The Weight of the Survivor’s Guilt
Surviving a layoff doesn’t feel like a victory when you’re haunted by the faces of colleagues who lost their jobs, some discovering their fate while on vacation. The emotional fallout is palpable as you’re wrestling with…

data.title: Where are vacation homes located in the US?
data.author: rufus_foreman
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了美国度假屋的分布情况。截至2023年，美国约有480万套度假屋，占总住房单位的3.5%。佛罗里达州拥有最多的度假屋，超过80万套，其次是加利福尼亚州和纽约州。按比例计算，新英格兰地区（缅因州、新罕布什尔州、佛蒙特州）的度假屋比例最高，而大平原地区比例最低。

度假屋的地理分布有几个明显模式：新英格兰、中西部北部、东南部和西部州较为集中。自1940年代以来，佛蒙特州、新罕布什尔州和缅因州一直是热门度假屋地点，而佛罗里达州和亚利桑那州在1960至1990年间显著增长。一些地区如新泽西州、罗德岛州和康涅狄格州的度假屋比例有所下降。

通过更细致的 census 数据，发现约53%的度假屋集中在20%以上住房为度假屋的区域，这些地区仅占总census tract的4%。这显示了度假屋在特定区域的高度集中性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： vacation home（度假屋）的趋势及其影响因素

不同观点：
• **空调与航空旅行的影响**：[snowwrestler] 认为空调的普及使得度假屋不再仅仅是为了避暑，而廉价航空使得富人可以更灵活地选择度假地点，无需固定拥有一处房产。这种变化可能解释了为何度假屋拥有率未随实际财富增长而增加。

• **度假屋的季节性与不可全年居住性**：[khuey] 指出，一些地区的度假屋（如缅因州和明尼苏达州的一些小木屋）不具备全年居住条件，冬天无法取暖或道路不通。这影响了这些房屋的实际使用价值。

• **度假屋的地理分布与人口密度关系**：[owenversteeg] 对佛罗里达州和缅因州的度假屋分布模式提出兴趣，特别是在人口密度高和低的地区之间存在不同的度假屋比例。建议绘制距离主要住宅的 census tract 图可能会提供更多见解。

• **度假屋定义与统计问题**：[stockresearcher] 和 [BrenBarn] 都提到，统计中的“度假屋”可能不包括通过 AirBnB 或 VRBO 出租的房屋，导致数据不完整。例如，洛杉矶的 AirBnB 数量远多于统计中的度假屋数量。

• **退休人员对度假屋市场的影响**：[unsnap_biceps] 和 [42772827] 提到，许多度假屋是由退休人员持有，尤其是佛罗里达和无所得税的州，这可能与年轻一代的购房偏好不同。

• **空置率与税务欺诈问题**：[tonymet] 认为，由于美国主要住宅的税务减免政策，实际空置率可能更高，尤其是在度假区。投资者可能通过虚假身份申报房屋占用以获取税务优惠。

• **其他特殊情况与投资因素**：[furyofantares] 猜测阿拉斯加的一些“度假屋”实际上是季节性工人的出租房。[terminalshort] 认为曼哈顿的许多“度假屋”实际上是外国富人用来存放资金的空置豪华单位。[phkahler] 提到一些退休人员在密歇根和佛罗里达（或亚利桑那州）之间根据季节移动，可能拥有两个度假屋。[tayo42] 则提到考虑在波多黎各购置度假屋以避开所得税。

补充讨论：
• **度假屋的价格与价值**：[relaxing] 指出，北部的一些“度假屋”实际上只是价值几千美元的荒地，这与高价的度假屋市场形成对比。

争议焦点：
• **度假屋的定义和统计数据的准确性**：不同用户质疑统计数据是否包括所有类型的度假屋，尤其是 AirBnB 或 VRBO 出租的房屋。
• **度假屋的实际使用情况与空置率**：一些用户认为，由于季节性因素和税务问题，许多度假屋实际上处于空置状态，未能充分发挥其预期功能。

As of 2023, the US has around 142.3 million housing units: roughly one home for every 2.4 people in the country. The vast majority of these homes – 127.5 million – are occupied. The remaining 14.8 million homes are vacant. Of these, around 4.8 million homes, or around 3.5% of the total, are vacant because they’re
seasonal, or vacation, homes
.
I’ve spent a lot of time writing about patterns of housing and home construction in the US, but virtually none of it has been looking at vacation homes specifically. I wanted to better understand patterns in the distribution of vacation homes in the US, for a few different reasons:
It tells us about patterns of recreation in the US: where are the popular vacation spots?
It tells us about patterns of elite consumption in the US: where do people who can afford it have second homes?
It points us to places that might have unique housing challenges due to very high demand from vacationers and tourists.
To look at US vacation homes, I used
Census data
, which tracks (to varying degrees of success, depending on the census year) the number of seasonal homes in the US going back to the 1940s.
1
Vacation homes in the US
The map below shows vacation homes in the US by state.
Florida leads the pack with over 800k vacation homes, followed by California at 360k and New York at 309k. Michigan (at 260k) and Texas (at 201k) round out the top five. At the bottom of the list, you have several Great Plains states: Kansas at 12.9k, South Dakota at 13.7k, and North Dakota at 11.6k.
There’s a few interesting patterns observable on this map — the dominance of Florida, the relative popularity of Midwest states like Michican and Wisconsin as a place for vacation homes, the fact that Alaska has nearly as many vacation homes as Hawaii — but to a large extent this map is a population map. 4 of the top 5 states for vacation homes are also in the top 5 by overall population (only Michigan breaks this trend, coming in at number 10 in overall population). To account for this, we can look at the fraction of homes in each state that are vacation homes.
By percentages, the pattern changes somewhat. Florida still ranks highly, with over 8% vacation homes, but it's soundly beaten by the New England states of Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont, which have 15.6%, 10.2%, and 15.1% vacation homes respectively. Even Delaware (8.6%) and Alaska (8.9%) have a greater fraction of vacation homes than Florida does. Michigan (5.7%) is now closer to the middle of the pack, along with places like Idaho (6.2%) and Arizona (5.5%). Great Plains states are still near the bottom (Kansas at 1%, Nebraska at 1.8%), but the state with the lowest fraction of vacation homes is actually Illinois at 0.8%.
At a high level, vacation homes are common in a few geographic regions: New England (Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont), the upper Midwest (Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan), the Southeast (Florida, the Carolinas), and the Western states between the Great Plains and the West Coast (Wyoming, Idaho, Utah, Arizona).
How have these patterns changed over time? The chart below shows the total number of vacation homes by state and year.
And this chart shows the fraction of homes that are seasonal by state over time:
Some states have always been popular places to have vacation homes: Vermont, New Hampshire, and Maine have led the pack continuously since the 1940s. Some states have gotten more popular over time. Florida and Arizona increased in popularity substantially between 1960 and 1990, presumably due to the spread of air conditioning (and the construction of places like Disney World). Western states like Montana, Idaho, and Wyoming also get more popular over time.
And a few states have gone down in popularity. New Jersey, Rhode Island, and Connecticut have all fallen in the fraction of homes that are vacation homes. But most states have stayed at relatively similar fractions of vacation homes over time, outside of a broad trend of vacation homes getting more popular in the US as a whole and percentages gradually ticking up everywhere.
Vacation homes by census tract
State-level data can reveal broad patterns in seasonal homes in the US, but we can get a better sense of where specifically the popular vacation spots are by looking at more granular data. The map below shows every census tract in the US where vacation homes are 20% or more of the total number of housing units. This is a small fraction of overall census tracts — 3,372 out of over 85,000 census tracts in the US, or around 4% of the total. But 53% of all vacation homes in the US are in such tracts.

主要讨论点：冠状动脉钙化（CAC）扫描及其在心脏病风险评估中的作用

不同观点：
• **支持CAC扫描的实用性**：
  - [crdioptnt] 通过CAC扫描发现了严重的心脏动脉阻塞，尽管之前没有明显症状，认为CAC扫描可以救命。
  - [jeremy151] 通过CAC扫描发现了高风险，并及时进行了他汀类药物治疗，认为该测试对风险分层非常有帮助。
  - [jboggan] 以低成本进行了CAC扫描，发现了自身独特的解剖结构和潜在风险，认为扫描可以预防灾难性疾病。

• **质疑CAC扫描的必要性**：
  - [wrs] 指出钙化斑块通常不易脱落，除非有显著狭窄，否则高钙分数并不总是与风险相关，建议通过CT血管造影进一步确认。
  - [Aurornis] 提到CAC扫描在某些网络社区中被误用和误解，认为低或零结果不能证明高胆固醇无害。

• **替代或补充测试的建议**：
  - [brandonb] 建议在进行CAC扫描前，先进行ApoB、Lp(a)、hs-CRP、HbA1c和eGFR等测试，认为这些测试可以评估软斑块的积累风险，并且大多数风险因素可以通过生活方式和药物进行调整。
  - [TechDebtDevin] 建议如果担心心脏病风险，可以自行支付CAC扫描费用，并进行Lp(a)测试以更好地了解胆固醇处理情况。

补充讨论：
• **医疗系统差异**：
  - [smath] 提到在美国需要医生处方和保险才能进行诊断测试，而在印度则较为自由，质疑美国是否存在法律或经济原因限制这种商业模式。

• **生活习惯与抗氧化剂的作用**：
  - [breadwinner] 强调抗氧化剂和绿茶的作用，认为氧化胆固醇而非胆固醇本身导致动脉粥样硬化，并指出他汀类药物可能带来的副作用。

• **个人经历和经验分享**：
  - [balderdash] 提到医学进步需要10-20年才能普及，感到有些沮丧。
  - [rsanek] 通过CAC扫描发现了其他严重问题，建议年轻人群体也可以考虑进行该测试。
  - [klipklop] 对测试结果的实际作用表示困惑，询问斑块是否可以逆转。
  - [lawls] 钙分数为零但有家族性高胆固醇，询问是否是好结果。

争议焦点：
• CAC扫描是否总是与心脏病风险相关，以及其在风险评估中的准确性和必要性。
• 如何解读CAC扫描结果，尤其是在某些网络社区中对该测试的误用和误解。

data.title: Simplify, then add delightness: On designing for children
data.author: shaneos
data.article_summary: Shane O'Sullivan 总结了为儿童设计应用程序（如 Kidz Fun Art）的几个关键原则，强调了与成人应用的不同。首先，尽量减少文字使用，因为儿童，尤其是8岁以下的孩子，阅读能力有限，且文字占据空间影响美观。其次，工具应与操作对象放在一起，并提供明显提示，避免使用菜单。第三，错误应易于纠正，如设置撤销按钮和软删除功能，以防止孩子因误操作失去作品。此外，设计应适时引导孩子寻求成人帮助，并减少对精细运动控制的要求。最后，避免使用广告 monetization，且不应让儿童在应用内花钱。这些原则旨在提升儿童应用的易用性和愉悦感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何设计适合儿童的交互界面，特别是触屏界面的使用及其对儿童的影响。

不同观点：
• Pensacola认为，尽管孩子们喜欢触觉体验，但将2D应用程序设计得像真实物体一样可能会导致过度依赖屏幕，而不是与现实世界的物理物体互动。这引发了对是否应让儿童过早接触屏幕的担忧。
  
• jrm4指出，触屏界面本质上是“儿童级别”的，这并不一定是坏事，但可能限制了可以完成的任务的复杂性和实用性。他还提到，如果任务是重复性的，可能根本不需要屏幕，特别是在汽车中应减少使用。

• danjl认为，这些为儿童设计的原则其实适用于所有年龄段，类似于为残障用户设计往往对所有人都更好。他引用了Good Grips的例子来说明这一点。

• prats226提到，有人建议尽量不让孩子过早接触屏幕，这与文章中提到的做法形成对比，显示出育儿建议中的矛盾。

• M95D认为，文中的现代用户界面看起来像是为成年人设计的，暗示这些设计原则可能不仅限于儿童。

• card_zero的关注点在细节上，对文中彩虹图案包含棕色感到 delight（欣喜）。

• preordained对“delightfulness”这个词的使用提出质疑，认为“delight”是更自然的表达，并对“delightness”作为替代词提出异议。

• hluska从育儿角度出发，强烈反对文中关于文本对儿童不利的观点。他认为，文本是语言的视觉 representation（表现），如果孩子觉得文本“令人反感”，那是因为成人没有正确引导他们与文本互动。他还强调了家庭中推广书面语言的重要性，并指出早期教育对孩子阅读能力发展的关键作用。

• 争议的焦点在于是否应让儿童过早接触屏幕和触屏界面，以及文本在儿童学习中的角色和重要性。

44711745.article_content:
Shane O'Sullivan
Technical
July 28, 2025
July 28, 2025
12 Minutes
I’ve been building Kidz Fun Art (
web
,
iPad
&
Windows
) since 2021, so 4 years at time of writing. It’s a tablet optimized application intended to be used by children of all ages – my daughters were 3 and 5 when I started, and are 7 and 9 now, so I’ve seen how they use it almost daily at various ages. I’ve learned a few things about designing for their usability and how it differs from some more common patterns found in adult focused applications.
Topics Covered
Minimize Text Use
Show, Co-locate and Hint tools
Mistakes should be easy to fix
Know when to involve an adult
Reduce the need for fine motor control
Try to solve Palm Rejection
Simplify, then add delight(ness)
Maintain visual context when changing state
Monetize without ads, or not at all
Plan for app growth without social sharing
Children should never spend money
Epilogue
Minimize Text Use
If you want kids under 8 to use your app, find a way to communicate all its primary functions with as little text as possible.
Text does not actually provide guidance to a large percentage of your user base as they can’t read it
Text takes up valuable space that could be used for better graphics or aesthetically pleasing empty space
Text is visually unattractive and off-putting to most children.
In the image below, note that there is not a single piece of text.  While secondary and tertiary features sometimes require text, do what you can to make all primary controls text-free.
Show, Co-locate and Hint tools
Adult focused apps often have menus where the user must know to hunt and peck for the features they need. This is not well suited to younger users. I’ve found that it works much better to design ways to co-locate tools with the objects on which they are to be used.
For example, if a user wants to select and rotate part of the image, place the control for rotating directly on or next to the selected area, not far away in a control bar or menu.
Place tools for manipulating objects directly on top of the objects, with large and obvious hit targets.  Feedback from my in-house testers was that putting things like rotation controls on the border of a selected area (like most paint apps) was not a good affordance, whereas overlaying a circle on top of the object to be rotated was immediately obvious.
If the available controls cannot be shown due to space constraints, find a way to hint at their existence in a way that does not require reading or tool tips.
The image above shows my attempt at gently suggesting to the user that there is a menu hidden under each of these buttons if they click a second time.  A key point for avoiding a messy UI that is overly noisy is to only show any given hint a small number of times, ideally just once.
Mistakes should be easy to fix
Kids make mistakes, they mess around and generally use the app in every way you never thought of.  They are naturally inquisitive and will tap, drag, slap, spit on and high five the screen at any given moment.  In all cases, but especially if they are creating content, you should try at all times to make any actions quick and easy to reverse (I need to better here, and my next mini-project is aimed at improving this for Kidz Fun Art).  Some ideas:
Have an undo button placed prominently, and a redo button of course. This means building to support a stack of states, which definitely complicates things, but your app will be far less frustrating with these.
Use soft deletes, so the user can undo an accidental deletion.  Nothing is more likely to make a kid never come back to your app than accidentally hard deleting something they’d spent hours creating and were about to proudly show their parents.  This happened a year ago to one of my daughters, full on tears ensued and if it wasn’t their dad building the app that would’ve been the end of their usage of it.  Safe to say I was up until 2am working on the fix, feeling like an absolute piece of shit. Don’t be that person.
Clean up the soft deletes at some point. I tend to do this after a few days, by which time the child has likely forgotten all about it. No need to keep the data forever. It bloats local storage and is just better for privacy all round.
Know when to involve an adult
If you have features aimed at older kids, your app will likely have stronger retention and usage of more advanced features if you encourage the child to involve the parent at the right times.
Use graphics as much as possible for these prompts, like in the example below. Once the user confirms that they are able to handle what comes next, it’s OK to use a bit more text than you normally would.
To reduce frustration for the user, for any single feature, only request the help of an adult once.  This will require you to store the fact that you did so on a per-feature basis either locally, remotely or both.
Reduce the need for fine motor control
Younger children’s motor control is not as developed as that of older childre

data.title: The Rise of Vibeinsecurity
data.author: matosdfm
data.article_summary: 文章描述了2035年由于人工智能（AI）和大型语言模型（LLM）的普及，编程变得极其简单，导致人人皆可开发应用。然而，这种快速开发也带来了大量安全漏洞，应用被迅速破解。文章提到，过去十年中，由于"氛围编码"（vibecoding）的兴起，软件开发岗位减少，许多开发者失业，而新手开发的大量应用由于安全措施不足而被黑客攻击。黑客利用AI扩大攻击规模，导致网络安全问题严重，隐私几乎消失。文章最后提出反思：如果情况不如此发展，是否会有不同结果？文章还宣传了2025年9月在里斯本举行的HackAIcon大会，探讨如何在AI时代应对这些挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对未来网络安全和当前安全实践的看法

不同观点：
• [righthand] 认为当前我们已经在面临严重的安全问题，比如将个人身份信息 (PII) 泄露给大公司，以及许多安全/IT部门其实并不真正了解安全。他指出，自己的IT部门在过去一年里由于不断改进“安全”措施，要求其观看了5个反钓鱼培训视频，而这还是在LLMs（大型语言模型）广泛应用之前。这暗示当前的安全措施无效且繁琐。

• [blamestross] 则聚焦于技术进步对黑客行为的影响，认为曾经在科幻作品中看似玩笑的“黑客行为”因为LLMs的兴起而变得可行。他的观点强调了技术进步（特别是LLMs）对网络安全领域的深远影响，暗示未来的安全威胁会变得更加复杂和严峻。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于对当前安全实践的有效性和未来技术影响的看法。一方面，[righthand] 对当前的安全实践持批评态度，认为即便没有LLMs，安全问题已经十分严重；另一方面，[blamestross] 则关注LLMs对黑客行为的潜在影响，认为技术进步会带来新的安全挑战。

• [righthand] 提到的反钓鱼培训和安全软件 upsell 问题，指向了当前许多组织在网络安全上的表面功夫和商业驱动，而非真正有效的安全防护。这与 [blamestross] 对未来技术影响的关注点有所不同，但两者都对现有的网络安全体系表示了不满。

Because we'll be discussing how to avoid this future at HackAIcon. Hosted in Lisbon, on the 25th of September, 2025. The best of the best will be there discussing how to hack in the age of AI and how to hack AI.

The year is 2035.
Everyone can code
The last decade brought the advent of vibecoding. LLM tokens are dirt cheap. Context windows became huge. And with that, everyone is shipping code.
A lot of it.
Your old roommate built an AI app that compliments your outfits.
Your uncle made a Slack bot that tells jokes in Elvish.
Your 9-year-old niece? She's launching a fintech API.
This led to an explosion of creativity. Anyone, anywhere, became a developer.
The first to get hurt were the software devs. Junior roles start drying up.
"Sorry, but you can't even set up a 10 endpoint API in under 5 minutes. We'll move on with other candidates."
they said.
Then layoffs happened. Mid-levels were hit. Many lost their jobs. Some went to Bali on a spiritual retreat. Others opened bakeries. Some bought land with the money of their latest exit and built a ranch.
Anyone could build apps. So why pay devs to do it?
At the same time, something unusual happened.
The number of applications getting hacked increased. A lot.
And they were getting hacked faster and faster. Vibe coded apps were getting hacked one second after deployment.
Seems that all these new apps were built hastily - too hastily.
They left exposed API keys. Hard-coded secrets. Default credentials on database logins.
AI could vibe your app. But who's securing it?
The internet was flooded with rushed, half-baked apps. And that's when the crackers moved in.
Not just the usual suspects.
Now it's
Vibe Hackers:
They came from all backgrounds.
Bored teens with ChatGPT jailbreaks.
Ex-designers turned exploit lords.
Laid-off devs who know exactly where to look.
These vibe hackers were using AI to scale attacks.
Vibecoding led to widespread vulnerabilities, so many that conventional hackers couldn't keep up. And the same way AI democratized building - it also democratized hacking.
And just like that, vibe insecurity was born.
Anyone's vibes could build any app, and with it came a host of vulnerabilities. Too many to keep up with. Apps that vibe, but don't survive.
Literally every domain on the internet was being probed for vulnerabilities. Attacks were so frequent that authorities couldn't keep up. You'd see people advertising their vibehacking services on LinkedIn: there were simply too many people to arrest, so advertising your services became commonplace.
For many industries it became an endless cycle: you launch a new version of your app, it's used, it's hacked, and then someone else comes and does it again with the promise of this time being unhackable. Needless to say, they weren't.
Privacy simply disappeared.
Everyone knows what you ate.
Everyone knows where you went.
Hell, everyone knows what you text.
But of course - it's a worthy trade-off, as now everyone can build. But some still dared to wonder:
What if things wouldn't be this way?

data.article_summary: 在黄石国家公园的一个温泉中，研究人员发现了一种能够同时利用氧气和硫磺进行呼吸的微生物，这打破了传统认知。通常，生命体要么使用氧气（有氧呼吸），要么使用其他元素如硫磺（无氧呼吸）来获取能量。由于氧气对许多无氧呼吸的生命形式具有毒性，传统观点认为这两种代谢方式不能同时进行。然而，这种微生物却能同时进行有氧和无氧代谢，为理解生命如何在远古时期从无氧环境适应富氧环境提供了新线索。该发现挑战了细胞呼吸的传统界限，并可能帮助科学家更好地理解微生物多样性和代谢的潜力。研究成果发表在《Nature Communications》上。

By

In a hot spring at Yellowstone National Park, a microbe does something that life shouldn’t be able to do: It breathes oxygen and sulfur at the same time.

Grand Prismatic Spring at Yellowstone National Park has the kind of chaotic chemistry — with both oxygen-rich and oxygen-free areas — that may support dual respiration.

Take a deep breath. A flow of air has rushed into your lungs, where the oxygen moves into your bloodstream, fueling metabolic fires in cells throughout your body. You, being an aerobic organism, use oxygen as the cellular spark that frees molecular energy from the food you eat. But not all organisms on the planet live or breathe this way. Instead of using oxygen to harvest energy, many single-celled life-forms that live in environments far from oxygen’s reach, such as deep-sea hydrothermal vents or stygian crevices in the soil, wield other elements to respire and unlock energy.
This physical separation of the oxygen-rich and oxygen-free worlds is not merely a matter of life utilizing available resources; it’s a biochemical necessity. Oxygen doesn’t play nice with the metabolic pathways that make it possible to respire with the use of other elements, such as sulfur or manganese. It gives aerobes like us life, but for many anaerobes, or creatures that respire without oxygen, oxygen is a toxin that reacts with and damages their specialized molecular machinery.
“Oxygen — we love it, of course,” said
Courtney Stairs
, an evolutionary biologist at Lund University in Sweden. “But it’s actually a pretty harmful molecule for most of life on our planet, and even ourselves. We have ways to mitigate the negative effects of oxygen. So we can’t imagine life without it, but life is actually quite hard with it.”
For the first couple billion years of life on Earth, organisms avoided this predicament altogether. Back then, the air and oceans were mostly devoid of oxygen, so life was almost entirely anaerobic, or non-oxygen-breathing. Then, around 2.7 billion years ago, the seas filled with industrious, photosynthetic cyanobacteria. They had invented a way to turn sunlight into sugar and oxygen, and they flourished. Over hundreds of millions of years, their accumulated breathing filled the atmosphere and oceans with oxygen. This so-called Great Oxidation Event was
a pivotal transformation
in the biosphere and the physical chemistry of Earth’s atmosphere and oceans. In this new environment, aerobic respiration evolved to dominate the world.
An ongoing mystery for researchers is how life navigated the shift from anaerobic to aerobic respiration; so much microbial biodiversity had to adapt to a world filled with what was once a biochemical bane. Now researchers have fresh insight into what that transition could have looked like billions of years ago, gleaned from an organism living today. A bacterium that researchers collected from the cauldron of a Yellowstone National Park hot spring does something that life really shouldn’t be able to do: It runs
aerobic and anaerobic metabolism
s simultaneously. It breathes oxygen and sulfur at the same time.
The findings “remind us yet again of just how much we still have to learn about microbial diversity and metabolism,” said
Natalia Mrnjavac
, a graduate student in evolutionary microbiology at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf in Germany who was not involved in the study. “And for someone who loves microbes, that is thrilling.”
The findings, which were published earlier this year in
Nature Communications
, challenge assumptions about the limits of cellular respiration and may give researchers a model for understanding how life walks the edge of paradise and poison.
Metabolic Tricks
It has long been known that life-forms have evolved ways of alternating between aerobic and anaerobic respiration, for instance as a last resort when oxygen levels are low. But because oxygen disrupts anaerobic respiration, many researchers assumed that cells couldn’t grow while using both processes at the same time.
So when
Eric Boyd
, a microbiologist at Montana State University in Bozeman, and his colleagues uncovered reports from the late 1990s and early 2000s suggesting that some bacteria might be doing just that, their curiosity was piqued. GLM-4.5: Reasoning, Coding, and Agentic Abililties
Our latest frontier model series, excels in reasoning, coding and agentic tasks.
Try it at Z.ai
Call it at Z.ai API

Today, we introduce two new GLM family members: GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.5-Air — our latest flagship models. GLM-4.5 is built with 355 billion total parameters and 32 billion active parameters, and GLM-4.5-Air with 106 billion total parameters and 12 billion active parameters. Both are designed to unify reasoning, coding, and agentic capabilities into a single model in order to satisfy more and more complicated requirements of fast rising agentic applications.
Both GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.5-Air are hybrid reasoning models, offering:
thinking
mode for complex reasoning and tool using, and
non-thinking
mode for instant responses. They are available on
Z.ai
,
Z.ai API
and open-weights are avaiable at
HuggingFace
and
ModelScope
.
Background:
LLM always targets at achieving human-level cognitive capabilities across a wide range of domains, rather than designed for specific tasks. As a good LLM model, it is necessary to deal with general problem solving, generalization, commen sense reasoning, and self-improvement. In the past five years, OpenAI's GPT-3 learns commen-sense knowledge, and o1 uses reinforcement learning to think before respond, significantly improving reasoning skills in coding, data analysis, and complex math. However, the resultant models are still not really general: some of them are good at coding, some good at math, and some good at reasoning, but none of them could achieve the best performance across all the different tasks. GLM-4.5 makes efforts toward the goal of unifying all the different capabilities.
Overall Performance
We compare GLM-4.5 with various models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, Alibaba, Moonshot, and DeepSeek on 12 benchmarks covering agentic (3), reasoning (7), and Coding (2). Overall, GLM-4.5 is ranked at the 3rd place and GLM-4.5 Air is ranked at the 6th.
Agentic Tasks
GLM-4.5 is a foundation model optimized for agentic tasks. It provides 128k context length and native function calling capacity. We measure its agent ability on 𝜏-bench and BFCL-v3 (Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard v3). On both benchmarks, GLM-4.5 matches the performance of Claude 4 Sonnet.
Web browsing is a popular agentic application that requires complex reasoning and multi-turn tool using. We evaluate GLM-4.5 on the
BrowseComp
benchmark, a challenging benchmark for web browsing that consists of complicated questions that expect short answers. With access to the web browsing tool, GLM-4.5 gives correct answers for 26.4% of all questions, clearly outperforming Claude-4-Opus (18.8%) and close to o4-mini-high (28.3%). Below the figure shows the test-time scaling accuracy of GLM-4.5 on the BrowseComp.

data.author: MBCook
data.article_summary: 文章报道了首个100%有效的HIV预防药物——lenacapavir（品牌名Yeztugo）获得批准并推广全球。该药物由Gilead Sciences开发，通过每半年注射一次提供接近100%的保护。Gilead与全球基金合作，放弃药物的专利使用费，计划在三年内向全球基金支持的国家提供足够剂量，帮助两百万高风险人群预防HIV。同时，Gilead还与多家仿制药厂商签署无专利授权协议，以确保药物在120个高发病率、资源有限的国家可负担且可获得。该药物的推出被视为终结HIV流行的重要里程碑。

Infectious Diseases
The first 100% effective HIV prevention drug is approved and going global
By
Bronwyn Thompson
July 26, 2025

The first 100% effective HIV prevention drug is approved and going global
Not for profit: Gilead, with the Global fund, is waving royalties from the breakthrough drug to reach two million people worldwide
Depositphotos
